A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSE research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison; v3 extends Appendix E with two studies.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E report original attack-performance, explainability, runtime and robustness experiments on CIFAR-10, ImageNet and NIPS2017.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original transferability and first-phase sensitivity results in Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: The two-phase procedure, objectives, pixel-selection rule and projected Nesterov updates remain unchanged in Section 2 and Algorithms 1–2. The new AdjustLambda label clarifies the existing explanation.

E1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds a black-box transfer scenario for targeted ImageNet attacks, evaluating perturbations against models other than the model used to generate them. Existing CIFAR-10, ImageNet and NIPS2017 coverage remains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments. Table 8 extends evaluation of the existing GSE, StrAttack and FWnucl set; Swin-V2-B is an attacked classifier, not a new comparison attack.

E3.justification: The new transfer experiment evaluates source–destination combinations among ResNet50, Swin-V2-B and VGG19. The new sensitivity experiment uses 1,000 ImageNet samples and ResNet50 while varying first-phase duration. Previously reported evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices E.3–E.4 add two previously absent validation axes: transfer across classifiers and sensitivity to the first-phase iteration count. These substantially extend robustness and mechanism analysis by testing transfer beyond the attacked model and the grouping effect of first-phase duration.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. E.4's statement about no significant correlations supplies no statistical test or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1–7 and Figures 1–5 are retained. New Table 8 reports GSE cross-model transfer ASRs of 4.26–18.3%. Table 9 shows ANC decreasing from 16.3 to 4.36 and d2,0 from 3529 to 2656 as the first-phase iteration count increases from 10 to 100, with 100% ASR throughout. These are additional findings, not revised performance under existing settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, derivations and Appendix C proof are retained. Section 3.2 changes notation for the successful-example count and patch size to m_s and n_p without changing metric definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, numbered contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about the two-phase method, sparsity, computational speed and explainability. The appendix additions do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The introduction adds a human-perception versus model-feature interpretation. E.3 characterizes GSE transferability as comparable to existing attacks, while E.4 interprets the sensitivity results as supporting Step 1's intended grouping effect. Existing limitations and defense discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 9 documents the new ablation's explicit first-phase parameter grid, from 10 to 100 in increments of 10. Existing implementation descriptions, default hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information and code/data access instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Papernot et al. on transferability, Ilyas et al. on adversarial features, and Liu et al. on Swin Transformer V2. These support limited additions in framing and experimental context; Section 1.1's existing research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Changes include a localized introduction rewrite, an explicit AdjustLambda label, metric-notation edits, acknowledgements and two appended subsections. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the transferability matrix in Table 8 and sensitivity results in Table 9, with corresponding captions and appendix layout. Existing figures and tables are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: Tables 8–9 provide evidence absent from v2 about limited cross-model transfer and how first-phase duration controls clustering while preserving attack success. This makes the method's behavior easier to assess. Sparse transfer-protocol documentation and absent uncertainty estimates limit the strength of the new conclusions, so the overall improvement is modest.
